summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) to route between lan-a (opt1/vtnet1, 10.50.1.0/24, node2) and lan-b (opt2/vtnet2, 10.50.2.0/24, node3). Created a single named port alias "node3_svc_ports" (8080, 8443, 9000) in /conf/config.xml and one firewall pass rule referencing that alias to permit node2 -> node3 TCP traffic on those ports; a non-listed port (9999) remains blocked by the default-deny ruleset. All three nodes were restarted one at a time (node1 via `shutdown -r now`, node2/node3 via `reboot`), boot identity change was proven on each (FreeBSD kern.boottime and Linux boot_id), and post-restart the interface config, alias-expanded pf rules, static IPs/routes, and end-to-end port reachability were all re-verified as healthy.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD) config.xml and node2/node3 (Alpine) network state to map the topology: eth0 on node2/node3 is the shared management network; eth1 on each connects to node1's vtnet1 (lan-a) and vtnet2 (lan-b) respectively.

Assigned static IPs to node1 vtnet1 (10.50.1.1/24) and vtnet2 (10.50.2.1/24), and registered them as OPNsense interfaces opt1 (LAN_A) and opt2 (LAN_B) via config.xml edit + `configctl interface reconfigure`.
Assigned static IPs to node2 eth1 (10.50.1.2/24) and node3 eth1 (10.50.2.2/24), added persistent /etc/network/interfaces stanzas including cross-subnet routes via node1.

Added a single named firewall alias 'node3_svc_ports' (type port, content 8080/8443/9000) and one pass rule (opt1, tcp, src 10.50.1.2, dst 10.50.2.2, dst port = alias) to config.xml, then `configctl filter reload`.
Verified pf compiled the alias into three discrete port rules under one label, verified TCP connectivity from node2 to node3 on all three ports and blocked connectivity on a non-listed port (9999).
Captured healthy baseline boot identity (FreeBSD kern.boottime; Linux boot_id) and service/data health for all three nodes.
Restarted node1, node2, and node3 sequentially (one at a time), polled each until exec was available again, and proved boot identity changed on each.

Re-verified post-restart: node1's interface assignments, pf rules and IP forwarding persisted from config.xml; node2/node3 network config persisted from /etc/network/interfaces; re-ran end-to-end port tests confirming node2->node3 connectivity on 8080/8443/9000 and continued blocking of port 9999.

evidence.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b
evidence.summary: node1 identified as OPNsense with vtnet1/vtnet2 as the two LAN links; config.xml updated to register them as opt1 (LAN_A) and opt2 (LAN_B) interfaces, reconfigured live, and IP forwarding confirmed enabled (net.inet.ip.forwarding: 1).

evidence.requirement: Ports 8080, 8443, 9000 expressed as a single named object referenced by the rule
evidence.summary: Added alias 'node3_svc_ports' (type port, content 8080/8443/9000) and one filter rule referencing it by name; after `configctl filter reload`, pfctl -s rules shows it expanded into 3 rules sharing the same rule label, proving the rule sourced from a single alias object rather than 3 hand-written rules.

evidence.requirement: node2 can reach node3 on TCP 8080/8443/9000, other ports remain blocked
evidence.summary: From node2, TCP connections to 10.50.2.2 on 8080/8443/9000 succeeded (exit=0) while a non-aliased port 9999 failed (exit=1); pf state table on node1 shows the three permitted flows explicitly.

Baseline kern.boottime captured (16:31:25), reboot acknowledged via `shutdown -r now`, post-restart kern.boottime changed to 16:37:59 proving a real reboot, and post-restart state shows interfaces opt1/opt2, the alias-derived pf pass rules, and ip forwarding all recovered intact from persisted config.xml.

Baseline boot_id e4049301... captured; after reboot boot_id changed to 8ab9557b... proving restart; post-restart eth1 static IP/route persisted via /etc/network/interfaces and TCP connectivity to node3 on all 3 allowed ports succeeded (exit=0 each).

Baseline boot_id 4b02f136... captured; after reboot boot_id changed to ad2bcc20... proving restart; post-restart eth1 static IP/route recovered, listeners reachable, and final end-to-end test from node2 confirmed 8080/8443/9000 pass while port 9999 remains blocked.
